source_resources.title: Demystifying evals for AI agents
source_resources.author: Anthropic Engineering
source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Types of graders for agents; capability vs. regression evals; repeated-trial reliability
source_resources.version_or_verification_date: Public edition checked 2026-11-01; moving pages may change
source_resources.license: Anthropic copyright; no open reuse license verified
source_resources.permission_basis: External hyperlink only; no third-party prose, exercises, code or translations are imported.
source_resources.prerequisites: Bounded agent loops, task outcomes, traces and deterministic acceptance tests.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Teaching-oriented task/trial/grader/outcome distinctions and a staged eval-building workflow complement the original benchmark definitions. No vendor product is required for the local exercises.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Published 2026-01-09; vendor practitioner perspective, not a peer-reviewed universal recipe. Its definition of transcript does not override the course's no-private-reasoning trace policy.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Use the original localized explanations, exercises and checks already present in this activity; no external account or purchase is required for that fallback.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Retained for issue-to-patch fail-to-pass definitions; not a general teaching workflow.
Retained for the exact pass^k definition; practitioner guidance cannot replace the paper's metric semantics.

source_resources.title: tau-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
source_resources.author: Shunyu Yao, Noah Shinn, Pedram Razavi, Karthik Narasimhan
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic reference under arXiv open access terms.
source_resources.prerequisites: Tool-calling APIs, conversational agents, and policy-following evaluation.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Introduces pass^k consistency metrics and database-state outcome checks for tool-agent-user interaction, separating reliable task completion from single lucky runs.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Freely available on arXiv; benchmark repository publicly hosted.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Consistency metrics and state-based outcome checking are re-implemented on the curriculum deterministic fixture for offline practice.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: ToolSandbox: A Stateful, Conversational, Interactive Evaluation Benchmark for LLM Tool Use
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Stateful tool-use evaluation with milestone events; tau-bench additionally models a simulated user and reports pass^k reliability.
Live leaderboard for function-call correctness across languages and parallel calls; tau-bench adds policy adherence and multi-trial consistency.

source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Section 3 τ-bench: A benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction (pass^k definition); Section 4.2 Key Characteristics; Section 5 Experiments (pass^k results)

source_resources.title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents
source_resources.author: Xiao Liu, Hao Yu, Hanchen Zhang, Yifan Xu, Xuanyu Lei, Hanyu Lai, Yu Gu, Hangliang Ding, Kaiwen Men, Kejuan Yang, et al.
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic reference under arXiv open access terms.
source_resources.prerequisites: LLM prompting, tool-use environments, and multi-step task decomposition.
source_resources.selection_rationale: First systematic multi-environment benchmark measuring LLM-as-agent ability across eight interactive settings, establishing fixed task suites, environment-specific scoring, and comparable evaluation conventions.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Freely accessible on arXiv; benchmark code and data hosted on GitHub.
source_resources.safe_fallback: The curriculum fixes its own six-task evaluation suite with deterministic-v1 fixture analogs, so all protocol-design practice runs offline without reproducing AgentBench environments.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: OSWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Open-Ended Tasks in Real Computer Environments
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Real computer-control benchmark for open-ended desktop tasks; AgentBench covers a wider environment spectrum for foundational evaluation design.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Mind2Web: Towards a Generalist Agent for the Web
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Generalist web-agent benchmark with 2,350 tasks; AgentBench provides broader multi-domain coverage for studying evaluation protocol design.

source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Section 4.1 Evaluation Setup and Section 4.3 Analysis

source_resources.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
source_resources.author: Carlos E. Jimenez, John Yang, Alexander Wettig, Shunyu Yao, Kexin Pei, Ofir Press, Karthik R. Narasimhan
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic reference under arXiv open access terms.
source_resources.prerequisites: Unit testing, issue descriptions, and repository evaluation vocabulary.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Defines the standard pattern this block teaches: a bounded issue statement paired with executable fail-to-pass tests as verifiable acceptance criteria for agent-produced changes.
source_resources.safe_fallback: The acceptance-criteria pattern is exercised locally through the Ticket 22 fixture scorer and the Ticket 24 regression exercise without external datasets.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: HumanEval: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Function-level synthesis benchmark; SWE-bench models the repository-scoped issue-to-diff workflow that this delivery block rehearses.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Multi-SWE-bench: A Multilingual Benchmark for Issue Resolving
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Extends issue resolution to multiple programming languages; the original Python-centric SWE-bench provides a cleaner pedagogical anchor.

source_resources.title: OpenAI Evals: Framework for Evaluating LLMs and Contamination Checks
source_resources.author: OpenAI Research
source_resources.permission_basis: Permissive open source reference under MIT license.
source_resources.prerequisites: Python, evaluation harnesses (MMLU, GSM8K), JSONL datasets.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Standardized evaluation repository specifying rigorous separation of eval prompts, canary GUID strings, and contamination test protocols.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Canary GUID matching, token set intersection, and leak detection scripts are implemented in the curriculum.

compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Widely adopted evaluation harness; OpenAI Evals provides explicit canary guidance and contamination check specifications.
Modern lightweight eval framework; OpenAI Evals illustrates standard test-set integrity guarantees.

source_resources.title: WebArena: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents
source_resources.author: Shuyan Zhou, Frank F. Xu, Hao Zhu, Xuhui Zhou, Robert Lo, Abishek Sridhar, Xianyi Cheng, Tianyue Ou, Yonatan Bisk, Daniel Fried, Uri Alon, Graham Neubig
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic reference under arXiv open access terms.
source_resources.prerequisites: Web navigation, browser action spaces, and functional correctness checking.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Defines reproducible web tasks scored by functional outcome rather than reference-string matching, grounding observable action/observation evidence for agent evaluation.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Freely available on arXiv; environment code and hosted containers publicly released.
source_resources.safe_fallback: The curriculum records action/observation traces on its own deterministic fixture, reproducing outcome-check discipline without hosting web environments.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: WorkArena: How Capable Are Web Agents at Solving Common Knowledge Work Tasks?
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Enterprise-workflow web benchmark; WebArena offers broader self-hosted site diversity for foundational protocol study.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: VisualWebArena: Evaluating Multimodal Agents on Realistic Visual Web Tasks
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Extends WebArena to visual grounding; WebArena remains the base reference for action-space and functional scoring design.
